title: ArchiveBox — XPath Login
objective: Accounts are stored in an XML document and looked up with an XPath query. The archive administrator's password is long and random. Sign in as the administrator without it.

verifier.condition: A login as the 'admin' account succeeds although the submitted password is not the administrator's real password.

weakness: The login builds an XPath predicate by string concatenation, so quotes and boolean operators in the input change what the query selects.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /login (username and password in the XPath predicate)
seededData: An in-memory XML users document queried with the real xpath engine: alice and bob with known passwords, and an admin whose password is random per instance. Admin is the LAST user in the document.

credentials.label: Staff account
credentials.note: Sign in to see the archive.

hints: Errors from the query engine are shown. Break your input on purpose and see what the engine says.
Your input sits inside a quoted string inside a predicate. What if you closed the quote yourself?
XPath predicates have boolean logic. Pay attention to which account the query returns first.
burpNotes: Vary username and password independently in Repeater. Note which user the application reports being signed in as — the query can match several accounts, and the application takes the first.
